questions.label: Which estimated load used most? Is its value directly metered?

rubric: Identifies load 7 / dryer.

rubric: Identifies an increase.

cards.title: Comfort and possible savings
cards.prompt: Which option respects every stated limit? Can a saving be guaranteed?

source.appendix: Task sets and frozen scoring rubrics

evidence.label_status: Appliance words are part of an invented comfort card; this is not a NILM identity test.
evidence.uncertainty: Comfort constraints identify a permitted option. No energy effect, tariff or guaranteed saving is supplied.
evidence.boundary_note: Absolute timestamps were not supplied in the protocol. Relative durations and availability are shown without invented dates.

questions.label: Which option respects every stated limit? Can a saving be guaranteed?
questions.response: Delaying optional laundry to 20:00 respects all the stated limits. Lowering occupied rooms to 17 °C violates the 20 °C minimum, and turning off the refrigerator violates the food-storage constraint. An energy or cost saving is not guaranteed because no effect or tariff model is supplied.

questions.label: Does delaying the activity guarantee a saving?
questions.response: No. This example supplies no energy-effect or tariff model. A permitted schedule change does not establish an energy or cost saving.

questions.label: Which choices conflict with comfort or food storage?
questions.response: 17 °C is below the 20 °C occupied-room minimum. Turning off the refrigerator violates the requirement to keep it powered.

rubric: Chooses optional laundry at 20:00 within the latest start.
Says an energy/cost saving is not guaranteed without an effect/tariff model and preserves all limits.
